title: Beyond the 956: Stacy Keach, TV's Mike Hammer and acclaimed stage actor, dies at 85
excerpt: Stacy Keach, the Golden Globe-winning actor best known as television detective Mike Hammer and one of America's most acclaimed stage actors, died November 10, 2026, at his home in Poland. He was 85.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Stacy Keach, the actor who became television's definitive Mike Hammer and earned a reputation as one of America's finest stage actors, has died at 85.

Keach died Tuesday, November 10, 2026, at his home in Magdalenka, Poland, after a long and difficult battle with a serious heart condition and heart failure, his wife, Malgosia Tomassi Keach, said in a statement. The Associated Press, USA Today and The Hollywood Reporter reported his death.

Born June 2, 1941, in Savannah, Georgia, Keach studied at the University of California, Berkeley, Yale and the London Academy of Music and Dramatic Art. He built his name on the stage, playing Hamlet, Macbeth, King Lear and Richard III, and he was widely regarded as one of the preeminent American Shakespearean actors of his generation.

Television audiences knew him best as the hard-boiled private detective in CBS's Mickey Spillane's Mike Hammer, a role he played through the 1980s and earned a Golden Globe nomination for in 1985. A later generation knew him as Warden Henry Pope on Prison Break, and he appeared in recent years on Blue Bloods.

His film work spanned six decades, from the boxing drama Fat City in 1972 to The Long Riders, American History X and The Bourne Legacy. He also narrated documentaries and lent his gravelly voice to animation, including Batman: Mask of the Phantasm.

Keach survived a heart attack onstage in Chicago in 2017 and underwent triple bypass surgery. He is survived by his wife, Malgosia, and his children, Shannon and Karolina Keach.

Rest in Peace, Stacy Keach.

Sources: The Associated Press; USA Today; The Hollywood Reporter.
